== The Age of Discovery ==

=== American Settlers ===

* John Glasgow, who landed in Antigua (recorded as “Antego”) in 1707–1708.<ref name="Filby">Filby, P. William, and Mary K. Meyer, ''Passenger and Immigration Lists Index: A Guide to Published Arrival Records of About 500,000 Passengers Who Came to the United States and Canada in the Seventeenth, Eighteenth, and Nineteenth Centuries''. 1982–1985 Cumulated Supplements in Four Volumes. Detroit, Michigan: Gale Research Co., 1985. Print. ISBN 0-8103-1795-8.</ref>
* Agnes Glasgow, who arrived in Pennsylvania in 1742.<ref name="Filby" />
* [[Glasgow-804|James Glasgow (1735–1788)]], who arrived in South Carolina in 1769.<ref name="Filby" />
* [[Glasgow-1654|David Glasgow (bef.1803-bef.1864)]], stated as having been born in Ireland in 1803 and died in Indiana on 13 March 1866. [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/G3NQ-1FY FamilySearch]
* [[Glasgow-2074|Edward Glasgow (abt.1795–1860)]], aged 17, who landed in Pennsylvania in 1812.<ref name="Filby" />
* Robert Glasgow, aged 25, who landed in New York in 1835.<ref name="Filby" />
* Dr Robert Glasgow, a slave-owner on St Vincent who moved to Scotland and left a significant physical legacy there in Montgreenan House.
* [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-540 Hugh Glasgow], who was born in Londonderry in about 1739 and died in Pennsylvania.
* [https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I958&tree=tree1 Alexander Glasgow], born in Pennsylvania in 1807. See also his [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-997 WikiTree profile].
* Agnes of Glasgow (1760–1780), a Scottish woman who became a figure of American folklore.<ref>[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_of_Glasgow “Agnes of Glasgow”, Wikipedia].</ref>
* [[Glasgow-2265|Maude Glasgow M.D. (abt.1869–1955)]], also reported as living from 1876 to 1955, was an early pioneer in public health and preventive medicine and an activist for equal rights.<ref>[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maude_Glasgow “Maude Glasgow”, Wikipedia].</ref>

=== New Zealand Settlers ===

* [[Glasgow-2605|Adam Glasgow (abt.1829–1880)]], who landed in Turakina, New Zealand, in 1840.
* John Glasgow, who landed in Wellington, New Zealand, in 1840.
* Robert Glasgow, who landed in Wellington, New Zealand, in 1840.
* Robert Glasgow, who arrived in Nelson, New Zealand, aboard the ship ''Bombay'' in 1842.
* Miss Jean Glasgow, a Scottish settler from Tillicoultry who travelled from Glasgow aboard the ship ''Strathfieldsaye'', arriving at Port Chalmers, Dunedin, Otago, South Island, New Zealand, on 29 April 1858.<ref>[http://www.yesteryears.co.nz/shipping/passlist.html ''New Zealand Yesteryears Passenger Lists 1800 to 1900''] (retrieved 26 March 2019).</ref>
* Mr D. Glasgow, a British settler who travelled from London aboard the ship ''Derwent Water'', arriving in Lyttelton, Canterbury, New Zealand, on 26 November 1861.<ref name="DerwentWater">[http://www.yesteryears.co.nz/shipping/passlist.htm ''New Zealand Yesteryears Passenger Lists 1800 to 1900''] (retrieved 17 October 2018).</ref>
* Mrs Glasgow, a British settler who travelled from London with four children aboard the ship ''Derwent Water'', arriving in Lyttelton, Canterbury, New Zealand, on 26 November 1861.<ref name="DerwentWater" />
* Robert Glasgow, who arrived in Auckland, New Zealand, aboard the ship ''Empress'' in 1865.
* Ann Glasgow, who arrived in Auckland, New Zealand, aboard the ship ''Empress'' in 1865.
* [[Glasgow-969|William James Glasgow (abt.1832–1886)]], who arrived in Auckland, New Zealand, aboard the ship ''Empress'' in 1865.
* Samuel Glasgow, who arrived in Auckland, New Zealand, aboard the ship ''Empress'' in 1865.
* Sarah Glasgow, who arrived in Auckland, New Zealand, aboard the ship ''Empress'' in 1865.

=== Notables ===

* '''(1568 x 1568)''' [[Glasgow-1030|Jhone Glasgow M.A.]], Minister of Kilbirnie from 1614 to 1629.
* '''(1614 x 1676)''' [[Glasgow-1101|Archibald Glasgow M.A. (bef.1614–)]].
* '''(1653 x 1721)''' [[Glasgow-1073|John Glasgow]], who married [[Cunningham-20924|Jean (Cunynghame) Glasgow]], was Minister of Kilbirnie in the Presbytery of Irvine from 1688 until his death in 1721.
* '''(1690 x 1764)''' [[Glasgow-1077|John Glasgow M.A.]], bailie in 1730 and three times provost between 1742 and 1752.
* '''(1690 x 1732)''' [[Glasgow-1136|Nathaniel Glasgow M.A.]].
* '''(1693 x 1693)''' [[Glasgow-1075|Robert Glasgow]], M.D., who married [[Cunningham-20924|Jean (Cunynghame) Glasgow]]. He was Chamberlain to the Viscount of Garnock and a surgeon at '''Kilbirnie'''.
* '''(1700 x 1718)''' [[Glasgow-3410|Jacob Glasgow M.A. (1700–)]].
* [[Glasgow-634|James Glasgow (1735–1819)]], North Carolina’s Secretary of State.
* '''(1747 x 1827)''' [[Glasgow-1076|Sir Robert Glasgow Jr]].
* '''(1786 x 1853)''' [[Glasgow-1220|William (Glasgow) Glass]], who pioneered the settlement that evolved into Edinburgh of the Seven Seas, '''the remotest community in the world'''. The rules he established remain a societal cornerstone of Tristan da Cunha, fostering communal unity, equitable employment opportunities and a culture of shared resources.
* '''(1792 x 1873)''' [[Glasgow-971|Alexander Glasgow]], a merchant from Lanarkshire who operated as ''Alexander Glasgow & Co.'' at 201 St Vincent Street.
** Alexander’s father’s birth records switch from “Glasgow” to “Glasfoord”, suggesting that [[Glasfoord-1|John Glassford of Dougalston and Whitehill]] may possibly have been a grandson of [[Glasgow-1030|Jhone Glasgow M.A. (abt.1568–)]].
* '''(1873–1945)''' [[Glasgow-473|Ellen Anderson Gholson Glasgow]], an American novelist who won the Pulitzer Prize for the Novel in 1942.
* '''(1876–1955)''' [[Glasgow-773|Thomas William Glasgow KCB CMG]].

== Surname Variants ==
In both Ireland and Scotland, the surname Glasgow is occasionally found as an Anglicised form of the Gaelic surname “MacCluskey”, originally “MacBhloscaidhe”, a patronymic derived from “Bloscadh”, meaning “Loud One”. It has also been identified as an Irish variant of the English family name Glasscock, which was once common in County Kildare.

* Elizabeth, Hannah, Samuel and William '''Glascow''', who settled in New England in 1760.
* Samuel Glascow, who landed in America between 1760 and 1763.<ref name="Filby" />
* Edward Glascow, who settled in New York in 1822.
* Anna '''Glasco''', aged 24, who landed in America in 1893.
* T. Glasco, aged 22, who landed in America in 1894.
